A CPU supports various features to accelerate program execution. SSE, AVX, 3DNOW, whatever. Basically, someone discovered that the Intel compiler was checking the name of the actual processor and then conveniently failing to use these extensions if the processor was not an Intel, even if the extensions were present and functional. This ended up just as you would expect; rival chips would score worse on code compiled with this compiler, because they were not Intel branded, and so (even if they supported the acceleration functions), the acceleration functions would not be used.
